name: orchestrator_routing
description: Asserts the orchestrator still dispatches the correct agents for each trigger type. Deterministic (no model, no API key), so this runs as a blocking gate on every PR. Scenarios marked critical encode capabilities the engineering system is required to have: if an edit to orchestrator/router.py drops one, the run fails and names the lost ability.

scenarios.description: A client/team transcript drives the full requirements pipeline; the dispatch set is the contract, so extras are flagged too.
Requirements extraction and architecture-drift detection must survive any routing edit — these are the client-facing artifacts of the pipeline.
Ordering is a correctness property, not a preference: requirements and decisions can only be extracted from an already-parsed transcript.
Coach sessions must still populate persistent memory plus commitment and concern tracking — the inputs to pre-meeting briefings.
Every PR must still get AI review and prompt-regression checking. Losing prompt_regression would silently disable the team's only automated guard against prompt quality decay.
Full PR dispatch set, including documentation generation.
Jira changes must keep feeding the traceability graph; without this, provenance in the Program Health dashboard degrades silently.
Stakeholder visibility: the weekly digest is a scheduled commitment, not an ad-hoc report.
Pre-meeting briefings must still be generated from coach memory.
Monday hygiene pass: stale-work detection and context packaging.
POC results must accumulate evidence and re-evaluate readiness rather than being read once and forgotten.
A manual trigger runs exactly the requested agent and nothing else — no surprise side effects when a human invokes one agent by hand.
An unrecognized trigger dispatches nothing instead of raising — an unknown webhook must not take the orchestrator down.
A manual trigger with no agent named is a no-op, not a fan-out to every agent.
